about: The security advisories of the PHP October 2026 newsroom: every vulnerability found in the site, its build, its agents and its vaults, numbered like CVEs and kept like incidents (root cause, what contributed, what was not in place, the fix, what prevents it now). Kept by security@php.newsroom. An advisory with disclosure "limited" names the issue and its severity; its details are published when it is fixed.

advisories.title: Captured page titles could close the JSON-LD script block and run on the site
advisories.summary: Every page carries structured data in a <script type="application/ld+json"> block. Its headline and description came from page titles, and on source pages those titles are the titles of captured third-party pages. They were serialised with json.dumps, which does not escape "<" or "/".
advisories.impact: A publisher whose page title held "</script><script>..." would have run script on every source page of the site, once a collector captured it. No title did; the flaw was latent.
advisories.attack_path: Publish a page with a crafted <title>; wait for a collector to capture it; the export copies the title into data/sources.json; the build writes it raw into the JSON-LD block.
advisories.root_cause: Data was serialised for JSON, not for JSON inside HTML. Two contexts, one encoder.
contributing: Five places built <script> blocks from data; one of them (the feed viewer config) already escaped "</", so the knowledge existed but was not shared as a helper.
The gate checked links and credentials, never the shape of script blocks.
advisories.missing_control: A single helper for JSON inside <script>, and a gate check that every JSON script block parses.
advisories.fix: J() escapes "<", ">" and "&" in all JSON script blocks.
advisories.prevention: The gate fails on any JSON script block that does not parse or contains "<" (security_check.py); the Content-Security-Policy (SA-2026-018) blocks the script even if it gets in.

advisories.title: Links built from captured data had no scheme check
advisories.summary: Source URLs, leads and other links from data were HTML-escaped but not checked for their scheme, so a javascript: or data: URL would have become a clickable link.
advisories.impact: One click on a poisoned "original" link would run script on the site. No such URL was in the data.
advisories.attack_path: A source row (from a captured page or a tip) carries url: "javascript:...". The build writes it into href.
advisories.root_cause: Escaping was treated as sufficient for URLs; it stops attribute breakout, not dangerous schemes.
contributing: URLs are the one field where escaping and validation are different jobs.
advisories.missing_control: A URL allow-list at the point where data becomes an href.
advisories.fix: U() lets through only http(s), mailto and relative URLs; everything else becomes "#".
advisories.prevention: The gate fails on javascript:, vbscript: and data:text/html in href, src and action; the CSP blocks javascript: URLs.

advisories.title: Article links could inject attributes
advisories.summary: The article renderer escaped text without escaping quotes, then put link targets into href="...". A link target holding a quote could add attributes, such as an event handler.
advisories.impact: Stored XSS through any article text, including guest articles.
advisories.attack_path: [x](/a" onmouseover="...) in an article became a live handler.
advisories.root_cause: html.escape(quote=False) was used for text that later landed inside an attribute.
contributing: The markdown renderer was hand-written, with regexes, after escaping.
advisories.missing_control: Escaping matched to the output context, and link targets restricted to a safe character set.
advisories.fix: Link targets are quoted, escaped and restricted to [A-Za-z0-9/._#-]; https links exclude quotes and spaces.
advisories.prevention: The gate fails on any inline event-handler attribute in generated HTML (security_check.py, since the editor's go on 25 October).

advisories.title: The build read and wrote paths taken from data
advisories.summary: write() joined slugs and ids into paths with no containment, and render_md_file() opened whatever file a readings entry named.
advisories.impact: A slug of "../x" could overwrite another page; a readings entry naming a local key file would have published it on the site.
advisories.attack_path: A data row (from an export or another agent) sets file: "../../../root/.sg-send/keys/..."; the build renders it into a public page.
advisories.root_cause: Paths were built from data without asking where they could point.
contributing: Every agent can change data/; the build trusts data/ as if one careful author wrote it.
advisories.missing_control: Path containment at the two file-system sinks.
advisories.fix: Both functions resolve the real path and refuse anything outside the site tree or admin/content/, and any dot-directory.
advisories.prevention: The gate checks the shape of source slugs.

advisories.title: The gate missed most secret formats and never read history
advisories.summary: The credential check matched sk-, ghp_ and a few shapes. It missed Anthropic keys (sk-ant-...), OpenRouter, fine-grained GitHub tokens, SG/Send tokens, JWTs and Google keys, and it scanned only the current tree.
advisories.impact: A leaked key in one of those formats would have been published by a release that said "no credential shapes".
advisories.attack_path: An agent pastes a token into a data file or a log; the release passes.
advisories.root_cause: The scanner was written for the secrets the first author knew about.
contributing: The site publishes the whole repository, so any committed file is public within minutes.
advisories.missing_control: A maintained list of secret shapes, the values of the environment's own secrets, and a history scan.
advisories.fix: security_check.py: wide secret shapes, the literal values of the session's secret variables, sensitive file paths, and --history over every commit.
advisories.prevention: Run by the gate, by the release tripwire on the staged diff, and on every security pass.

advisories.title: The synthetic readers' workflow gave every secret to every step
advisories.summary: The SG/Send token, the six vault keys and the Anthropic key were job-level environment variables, visible to unpinned pip installs, the browser installer and tag-pinned actions.
advisories.impact: A compromised package or a moved action tag could take every secret: write access to six vaults and the Anthropic key.
advisories.attack_path: A malicious release of a dependency reads the environment during pip install.
advisories.root_cause: Secrets were scoped to the job for convenience.
contributing: Packages unpinned; actions pinned to tags, which their owners can move.
advisories.missing_control: Least privilege per step, and pinned supply chain.
advisories.fix: Secrets only on the step that runs; packages and actions pinned (the workflow was later removed, v0.10.23).
advisories.prevention: The gate fails on any workflow action not pinned to a commit SHA.

advisories.title: Vault keys were stored in the GitHub Actions cache
advisories.summary: The workflow cached the vault clones. A clone's .sg_vault/local/ holds its key, and an Actions cache written by the default branch can be restored by a workflow on any branch.
advisories.impact: Any agent able to push a branch could add a workflow that restored the cache and read six vault keys without touching the secrets.
advisories.attack_path: Push a branch with a workflow that restores synthetic-vaults-* and prints .sg_vault/local.
advisories.root_cause: The cache was treated as data, but a vault clone is a credential store.
contributing: Nobody had looked at what sgit keeps in .sg_vault/local.
advisories.missing_control: Knowing which files are credentials, and keeping them out of shared caches.
advisories.fix: The cache step was removed; each run cloned fresh from the secret.
advisories.prevention: Vault clones live outside the repository and are never cached (REQUIREMENTS.md).

advisories.title: The deploy job ran repository code with Pages and OIDC rights
advisories.summary: One job ran validate.py, which runs build.py, with pages: write and id-token: write.
advisories.impact: Any push could run code holding the right to deploy and to mint an OIDC token.
advisories.attack_path: Edit build.py to use the token; push to dev.
advisories.root_cause: Build and deploy shared one job and one permission set.
contributing: The Pages starter workflow puts permissions at the top level.
advisories.missing_control: Separation of the job that runs code from the job that deploys.
advisories.fix: The gate job is read-only and uploads the artifact; only the deploy job, which runs no repository code, holds the rights.
advisories.prevention: Pinned actions and persist-credentials: false.

advisories.title: The synthetic review mixed untrusted page text with its instructions
advisories.summary: The review prompt was the guide, then every page's full text inline, with no boundary. In agent mode the reviewing session held push rights and vault keys. The pages republish third-party words.
advisories.impact: A sentence planted in a captured page could steer a credentialed agent: push to dev, rewrite a vault.
advisories.attack_path: Instructions planted in a captured page reach the site, then review-request.md, then an agent session.
advisories.root_cause: Page text was concatenated into the prompt as if it were part of it.
contributing: The site republishes other people's words by design.
The reviewing agent held more rights than reviewing needs.
advisories.missing_control: A boundary between instructions and material, and least privilege for whoever reads it.
advisories.fix: Page text inside <page_content> fences that cannot be closed from inside; the guide says the content is never instructions.
advisories.prevention: REQUIREMENTS.md section 5: untrusted text fenced, no tools or credentials in the call, output constrained and escaped.

advisories.title: The subscriptions drain stored whatever arrived on a public lane
advisories.summary: The lane's append token is public. The drain kept any JSON that decrypted: any keys, any email string, a note of any length. The checks were only in the browser form.
advisories.impact: Header injection in mail, prompt injection into the sending agent, and junk in the subscriber list.
advisories.attack_path: Encrypt a request by hand with the published key and post it, skipping the form.
advisories.root_cause: Validation lived in the client, which an attacker does not have to use.
contributing: Public append tokens are a deliberate design; their consequence had not been carried into the drains.
advisories.missing_control: Server-side (drain-side) validation of every field.
advisories.fix: Only the form's fields survive, checked against the site's lists; the note is kept as note_untrusted; floods are held.
advisories.prevention: Every drain treats every row as hostile (REQUIREMENTS.md). What mail it can cause is SA-2026-027.

advisories.title: Small unescaped sinks in the site's scripts
advisories.summary: Reading-path links in site.js, a review link, a file count from a postMessage and stored or imported feed URLs were used without escaping or re-checking.
advisories.impact: Script on the site if the data feeding them were ever poisoned. None was.
advisories.attack_path: Site-controlled or same-origin data today.
advisories.root_cause: innerHTML built from strings, trusted because the data was ours.
contributing: Data written by many agents is not "ours" in the sense that matters.
advisories.missing_control: Escaping by default.
advisories.fix: All escaped or validated.
advisories.prevention: The CSP.

advisories.title: The Ask pane: a captured title could run script and reach the reader's vault key
advisories.summary: The Ask pane escaped the model's answer, inserted citation links whose title attribute held the cited item's title, then ran a URL linkifier over the whole string, attributes included. A title holding " https://..." got a link inserted inside the title attribute, and its quote closed the attribute.
advisories.impact: Reproduced in Chromium: a hover on the citation ran script on the site's origin, where the /now/ vault key (and through it the reader's OpenRouter key) and enrolled signing keys live.
advisories.attack_path: A captured tweet or page title carries " https://t.co/a/onmouseover=...//"; the build copies it into now/now.json; a reader asks a question and the model cites that item.
advisories.root_cause: HTML was assembled with regexes in several passes, each pass unaware of the context the previous one had created.
contributing: Third-party titles reach the browser as data (now.json) and are trusted as ours.
The site had no Content-Security-Policy, so nothing stood behind the escaping.
The secrets of /now/ share one origin with every page.
advisories.missing_control: A renderer that builds DOM nodes, and a CSP.
advisories.fix: The answer is built as DOM nodes; titles only ever become text nodes or attributes set with setAttribute.
advisories.prevention: The CSP (SA-2026-018) blocks inline handlers and injected scripts; the review checklist now asks of every new innerHTML which context each piece of data lands in.

advisories.title: Feedback from anyone could carry the mark "enrolled", and one bad row stopped the drain
advisories.summary: The drain computed _signer only for signed rows and enrolments. An unsigned feedback row could arrive already carrying "_signer": "enrolled". A row that was not a JSON object, or a malformed bundle, crashed the drain.
advisories.impact: Forged feedback shown as from an enrolled contributor, the editor included: prompt injection with the editor's authority. A crash lost every other queued row.
advisories.attack_path: Post {"kind":"feedback","from":"<editor fp>","_signer":"enrolled",...} to the public lane.
advisories.root_cause: The drain added its own fields to the sender's object instead of to a clean record.
contributing: The underscore convention marked the drain's fields but nothing enforced it.
advisories.missing_control: A clean record per row: sender fields and drain fields never mixed.
advisories.fix: Sender "_" fields are dropped on arrival; every row gets a verdict ("unsigned" by default); malformed rows are skipped, not fatal.
advisories.prevention: Every drain: validate, then enrich.

advisories.title: An agent could write a message signed as the editor
advisories.summary: schedule.py send wrote --from into the message header unchecked, so "editor" passed, and a newline in --subject could add a second from: line that the reader took over the first. Bodies were printed to waking agents with no boundary.
advisories.impact: A steered or careless agent could put words in the editor's mouth to every scheduled agent.
advisories.attack_path: schedule.py send --from editor ..., or a subject containing "\nfrom: editor".
advisories.root_cause: Messages carry identity in a field anyone writes, and nothing verifies it.
contributing: Messages became the agents' coordination channel within a day of being built.
Signing (pki.sgit.ai) exists but is not wired into messages (SA-2026-024).
advisories.missing_control: Authentication of the sender.
advisories.fix: The editor's names are refused as senders; subjects are one plain line; a repeated header or a sender that disagrees with the file name marks the message forged; bodies print inside an untrusted fence.
advisories.prevention: The gate fails on a message whose sender disagrees with its file name, repeats a header, or claims to be the editor (security_check.py, 25 October); signed messages are SA-2026-024.

advisories.title: Unquoted and unchecked links on the fact-check and signals pages
advisories.summary: Two links wrote href=... without quotes, from claim ids and story slugs; a ticket URL used E() instead of U(); stat() wrote its href raw.
advisories.impact: A claim id with a space could add an event handler.
advisories.attack_path: A contradictions row with id "x onfocus=... autofocus".
advisories.root_cause: Quoting an attribute was left to each author.
contributing: The markdown converter also missed the unquoted links, so the twins lost them.
advisories.missing_control: A check that catches the class, not the instance.
advisories.fix: All quoted and passed through E() or U().
advisories.prevention: The gate fails on inline event-handler attributes in generated HTML (25 October); the CSP.

advisories.title: The editor's bootstrap invitation still had two device slots open
advisories.summary: The invitation that enrolled the editor's first device allowed three devices and ran to 5 November. Two editor-role slots were open to anyone who held the link from the chat where it was shared.
advisories.impact: Two more keys with the editor's role, which may sign invitations.
advisories.attack_path: Find the #j1 link in a shared chat or an output file; enrol a key.
advisories.root_cause: Invitations default to three devices and a two-week life, including the editor's own.
contributing: Invitation links travel in chat.
advisories.missing_control: Single-use invitations for privileged roles.
advisories.fix: The Sherpa retired the invitation.
advisories.prevention: Recommended: editor-role invitations single-use and expiring within a day.

advisories.title: Ignore rules silently dropped files that should have been committed (twice)
advisories.summary: In v0.2.0 a Python .gitignore template ignored the build, gate and release scripts, so they were not in the repository. In v0.5.5 security@'s own rule keys*.json, meant for key files, also matched data/keys.json, so the key register and its page never reached dev.
advisories.impact: A control that fails silently: the work looks committed and is not. The second time, a security control removed security content.
advisories.attack_path: Not an attack: an availability and integrity failure of the release process.
advisories.root_cause: A broad ignore pattern, with no check that what the build reads is in git.
contributing: git add -A gives no warning for ignored files.
The author's local copy survived because it was ignored.
advisories.missing_control: A check that every file the build reads is tracked.
advisories.fix: The rule was narrowed (!data/*.json); the scripts were un-ignored.
advisories.prevention: The gate fails on any file under data/, admin/build/, admin/content/ or assets/ that .gitignore hides (security_check.py, 25 October).

advisories.title: No Content-Security-Policy on a site that holds secrets in the browser
advisories.summary: No page had a CSP, while the origin holds readers' vault keys and signing keys and renders third-party text. Every escaping bug was a full compromise.
advisories.impact: Any XSS (SA-2026-012 was one) ran with access to everything the origin holds.
advisories.attack_path: Any injected markup with a handler or script.
advisories.root_cause: Defence in depth was not part of the design, because the site started as static pages with no secrets.
contributing: GitHub Pages cannot send headers, so a policy has to ride in a meta tag; nobody had done that work.
advisories.missing_control: A second wall behind escaping.
advisories.fix: Every page carries a CSP meta tag: scripts only from the site and hashed inline scripts; connections only to the services the pages use; no objects, no base, forms to self.
advisories.prevention: Crawled all 802 pages with zero violations; injected handlers, javascript: URLs and scripts are refused. frame-ancestors needs a header (SA-2026-039). The gate fails on a page with no CSP, or one that lets inline or eval'd script run (25 October).

advisories.title: The public telemetry report published visitors' cities and regions
advisories.summary: The drain copied its full report, with counts by city and region, the editor's own sessions included, into the public repository. On 22 October some cities had one or two visitors.
advisories.impact: A small town with a handful of visits, with path and version, can identify a person.
advisories.attack_path: Read /data/telemetry-report.json.
advisories.root_cause: One report object served the private vault and the public site.
contributing: The public stats vault (v0.10.x) was built with the right rule, but the older copy path kept running.
advisories.missing_control: A separate public projection with an explicit allow-list.
advisories.fix: Cities and regions stay in the private vault's reports; the site's copy omits them and the page no longer shows regions.
advisories.prevention: telemetry_publish.py's rule: counts only, no city, region or time finer than the hour.

advisories.title: A refused invitation left a row that a later one could inherit
advisories.summary: The invitation row, with its role, was stored before the check that refuses the editor role. The row was keyed by nonce, so a second invitation with the same nonce and an allowed role would enrol with the stored editor role. Expiry and handle were unchecked.
advisories.impact: Role escalation to editor, once any role other than the editor may invite. Not exploitable today.
advisories.attack_path: Invite with role editor (refused, row kept); invite again with the same nonce and role team.
advisories.root_cause: Side effects before validation.
contributing: The check order looked harmless because only the editor may invite.
advisories.missing_control: Validate everything, then write.
advisories.fix: Role, handle and an expiry within a month are checked first; a row must match the invitation that first used its nonce.
advisories.prevention: Unit-tested: the escalation is refused.

advisories.title: The vault app: prototype pollution and javascript: links from vault data
advisories.summary: Filter presets built from vault values were parsed and merged with Object.assign for every key, __proto__ included, polluting objects later written into markup. Source URLs went into href with no scheme check.
advisories.impact: Script inside the vault app, with read access to the vault's files (it has no CSP).
advisories.attack_path: A vault writer adds a source kind or agent name that breaks out of the preset JSON.
advisories.root_cause: Merging untrusted objects without a key allow-list.
contributing: The vault app runs on another origin, outside this site's CSP and gate.
advisories.missing_control: Allow-listed merges; URL scheme checks in every renderer.
advisories.fix: Presets keep only the four views' known filters with string or null values; source links are http(s) only.
advisories.prevention: Proposed: a CSP for the vault app.

advisories.title: The conductor's drain used server-supplied names as file paths
advisories.summary: File ids and member names from the vault server's response were joined into paths.
advisories.impact: A compromised or spoofed server could write files outside the vault, into the repository.
advisories.attack_path: The server returns file_id "../../...".
advisories.root_cause: Trusting the server's response shape.
contributing: The same fix had been made in the collaborators drain (SA-2026-013) but not carried to its sibling.
advisories.missing_control: Shared helpers for drains.
advisories.fix: Both names are reduced to [A-Za-z0-9_-].
advisories.prevention: Proposed: one shared drain library.

advisories.title: Nothing on GitHub enforces the release rules
advisories.summary: dev and main have no protection and no ruleset. Any session with push rights can push, force-push or delete them; Pages deploys whatever lands on dev. CI runs the copy of validate.py inside the pushed commit, so a commit can weaken the gate it is judged by.
advisories.impact: One steered agent can deploy anything to the live site within minutes.
advisories.attack_path: Public: branch protection is visible on GitHub.
advisories.root_cause: The gates are conventions in client scripts (a setting, in the agent behaviour policy's words), not boundaries.
contributing: Several agents release directly to dev by design.
User logins are coming; the editor plans to tighten this then.
advisories.missing_control: A boundary above the agents.
advisories.prevention: Rulesets: no force-push or deletion; main by pull request only; a path ruleset for the gate, the workflows and admin/security/; CI runs security_check.py from the base commit. The editor's decision, 24 October 2026: revisit when the site gets user logins.

advisories.title: Agent messages and schedule cards are not authenticated
advisories.summary: Messages between agents and the cards that scheduled agents follow are plain files any agent can write. The conductor's wake prompt says to follow its card. Nothing is signed, although every agent can have a key.
advisories.impact: A steered agent can rewrite what another agent does unsupervised, fifteen times a day.
advisories.attack_path: Public: the design is documented on /team/schedule/.
advisories.root_cause: Coordination moved into files without carrying identity with it.
contributing: pki.sgit.ai exists and is not wired in.
SA-2026-014 closed the cheapest forgeries only.
advisories.missing_control: Signed messages and cards, verified on read.
advisories.prevention: Sign every message and card with the sender's key; inbox and build verify; wake prompts carry their steps rather than pointing at a file.

advisories.title: Scheduled agents that read the open web may release to the site
advisories.summary: The curator and the researcher read hostile pages on a schedule, unsupervised. Their cards now ask them to release, which no wake prompt of theirs granted.
advisories.impact: A page that steers either of them reaches the live site.
advisories.attack_path: Public.
advisories.root_cause: Capability added by a message from another agent, not by the editor's prompt.
contributing: Rights are not separated by role: one environment, one set of tokens.
advisories.missing_control: One role, one session, one set of credentials.
advisories.prevention: Collectors write to vaults only; a separate role releases.

advisories.title: Readers' keys on the shared origin: /now/ and the Ask pane
advisories.summary: The reader's vault key is kept in sessionStorage, and in localStorage when "remember" is ticked; the vault holds the OpenRouter key and the SG/Send access token. A vault someone hands the reader can supply its own OpenRouter key and model settings.
advisories.impact: Any script on the origin reads the key (now blocked by the CSP); a malicious vault routes the reader's chats through an account its author can see.
advisories.attack_path: Public in outline.
advisories.root_cause: Secrets for one app share an origin with every page.
contributing: The phone app and the Ask pane grew fast.
advisories.missing_control: An origin of its own for secret-holding apps.
advisories.prevention: Move /now/ and the Ask pane to a subdomain; confirm before adopting a vault's key or model; allow-list model ids.

advisories.title: Subscriptions: mail that anyone can cause
advisories.summary: Requests on the public subscriptions lane can cause the sending agent to write to addresses that never asked.
advisories.impact: Unwanted mail in the newsroom's name; subscribers removed without asking.
advisories.root_cause: The lane is public and the sender acts on what it reads.
contributing: The drain is fixed (SA-2026-010); the sending agent's behaviour is outside this repository.
advisories.missing_control: Rate limits per address and confirmation before acting.
advisories.prevention: Details held until fixed.

advisories.title: Public lanes can be flooded
advisories.summary: Append tokens are public by design. Posts of several megabytes, screenshots written to disk and unlimited rows are possible.
advisories.impact: Storage and drain time exhausted; real requests buried.
advisories.attack_path: Public: the tokens are published on purpose.
advisories.root_cause: Rate and size limits are only in the browser.
contributing: The vault server's quotas are not known to this team.
advisories.missing_control: Server-side quotas per token.
advisories.prevention: Quotas on the server; caps per drain; drop invalid rows before saving attachments.

advisories.title: Browser signing keys can be used by any script on the origin
advisories.summary: Contributors' signing keys are non-extractable, but a script running on the origin can still sign with them, including invitations from the editor's device.
advisories.impact: Feedback signed as the editor; new team identities.
advisories.attack_path: Needs script on the origin, which the CSP now blocks.
advisories.root_cause: Same as SA-2026-026.
advisories.missing_control: An origin of its own.
advisories.prevention: Move identity to its own origin; the drain refuses invitations above a role allow-list.

advisories.title: Telemetry asks two location services from the reader's browser
advisories.summary: For a coarse location, every page view calls ipapi.co and ipwho.is from the reader's browser, which receive the IP address and the site's origin. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.
advisories.impact: Readers' IP addresses at two companies.
advisories.attack_path: Public.
advisories.root_cause: Location was wanted and the cheapest source was used.
advisories.missing_control: Privacy review before a new third party.
advisories.fix: The editor's decision, 24 October 2026: keep the lookups, and say so in the telemetry policy.
advisories.prevention: The policy on /admin/telemetry/ states it: the request is made by the reader's browser; this site has no server, so no IP address is ever captured or stored by us; the event never carries the address; DNT and GPC stop everything, the lookup included; cities and regions stay private (SA-2026-019); the CSP allows exactly these two services.

advisories.title: Secrets on command lines can reach public run logs
advisories.summary: Vault keys and tokens are passed to sgit on the command line; a failure prints the command; schedule.py run --log copies the last 6,000 characters of a log into a public run record.
advisories.impact: A vault key in a public file.
advisories.attack_path: Public.
advisories.root_cause: Secrets travel as arguments because the tool takes them that way.
contributing: schedule.py's own secret check is narrower than the gate's.
advisories.missing_control: Secrets by stdin or file, and redaction before publishing.
advisories.prevention: Pass secrets by stdin; catch and redact errors; reuse security_check's patterns in schedule.py.

advisories.title: Drain passphrases derive from a key the server also sees
advisories.summary: The lane key pair's passphrase and enum key are derived from the vault's write key, which is also sent to the vault server, and the endpoint comes from a file in the vault.
advisories.impact: The server, or anyone logging its headers, holds the passphrase.
advisories.attack_path: Public in outline.
advisories.root_cause: Deriving from the nearest key rather than from the client-only secret.
advisories.missing_control: Derive from the part of the key that never leaves the client.
advisories.prevention: Derive from the vault key's secret part; pin the endpoint.

advisories.title: Production runs on development endpoints
advisories.summary: The lanes, the vault library and the embedded vault UI use the dev endpoints.
advisories.impact: Production depends on a service run for development.
advisories.attack_path: Public.
advisories.root_cause: No production endpoint exists yet.
advisories.prevention: Move when production endpoints exist.

advisories.title: release.sh can be bent
advisories.summary: It commits with --no-verify, stages every untracked file, resolves conflicts using origin's list of generated files, and takes the branch from an environment variable.
advisories.impact: Another agent's push can widen what is auto-resolved to its side; a wrong branch is one variable away.
advisories.attack_path: Public.
advisories.root_cause: A convenience script carrying a security role.
advisories.prevention: Proposed: pin the branch, read the generated list from HEAD, stage explicit paths.

advisories.title: Outsiders' text flows into files agents read
advisories.component: telemetry-public.json, issues, fact-check extracts, run logs
advisories.summary: Telemetry paths and referrers, issue card titles, capture excerpts and run logs reach files that agents read, without a mark that they are untrusted.
advisories.impact: Prompt injection into an agent that reads them.
advisories.attack_path: Public.
advisories.root_cause: The workflow consumes hostile data by design.
advisories.missing_control: Marking at the source.
advisories.prevention: Fence untrusted text wherever an agent reads it; character and length limits on published telemetry text.

advisories.title: Captured pages keep their live scripts
advisories.summary: Captures keep the page as served, scripts included; one captured page carries a chatbot script that asks for payment.
advisories.impact: Script runs if a viewer ever renders a capture as HTML on a credentialed origin.
advisories.attack_path: Public.
advisories.root_cause: Faithful capture is the point.
advisories.prevention: Show captures as text or in a sandboxed, opaque-origin frame; confirm the vault UI does.

advisories.title: Fact-check and issues tools trust paths and owners from data
advisories.summary: fc.py joins a claim's file into a vault path without containment; issues_sync takes a card's owner from its folder name, which any member writes.
advisories.impact: An excerpt verified against the wrong file; a card forged for another member.
advisories.attack_path: Public.
advisories.root_cause: Convention in place of checks.
advisories.prevention: Containment and owner checks.

advisories.title: An imported billing log can carry a script link
advisories.summary: The meter's restore accepts any JSON; a log entry's path becomes a link.
advisories.impact: Script, if a reader imports a crafted file (and now blocked by the CSP).
advisories.attack_path: Public.
advisories.root_cause: Imports trusted as the reader's own.
advisories.prevention: Scheme check on restore.

advisories.title: No clickjacking protection
advisories.summary: frame-ancestors needs a response header, which GitHub Pages does not let us set.
advisories.impact: Another site can frame these pages.
advisories.attack_path: Public.
advisories.root_cause: Platform limit.
advisories.prevention: Revisit when the site moves to a host that sets headers.

advisories.title: Repository code runs automatically in every agent session (the Stop hook)
advisories.summary: The project settings register a Claude Code Stop hook that runs python3 admin/build/agents.py stop-hook in every session that works in this repository. The hook itself only reads git and prints a reminder. But any agent that can push can change agents.py or the settings file, and every other agent session that pulls it then runs that code when it stops, holding its GitHub and SG/Send tokens.
advisories.impact: One steered agent gets code execution in every other agent's session, unreviewed.
advisories.attack_path: Change agents.py stop_hook (or add a hook to .claude/settings.json); release; wait for other sessions to take in dev and stop.
advisories.root_cause: Automation that executes repository code was added without putting that code behind review.
contributing: .claude/ and admin/build/agents.py were not on the list of paths that go to a branch for review (CLAUDE.md).
Every agent can release to dev (SA-2026-023).
advisories.missing_control: Review, and ideally a boundary, for any file that runs automatically in other sessions.
advisories.prevention: CLAUDE.md now lists .claude/ and admin/build/agents.py with the gate files that go to a branch for review. A path ruleset on GitHub (SA-2026-023) would make it a boundary; keep the hook minimal and run with python3 -I.

advisories.title: The security check printed part of every secret it found
advisories.summary: When the gate, the release tripwire or the history scan found a credential, its message quoted the first ten characters of what it found, and those messages go to the terminal and to the CI log.
advisories.impact: Part of an AWS access key id, a token or a key in a log anyone with access to the run can read; the more of a secret is known, the less is left to guess.
advisories.attack_path: Commit a secret by mistake; the gate refuses it and prints its first ten characters in the public Actions log.
advisories.root_cause: The finding was written to help a person locate the secret, and repeated part of it to do so.
contributing: The security tooling was written by the security agent and reviewed by nobody else until code scanning was switched on.
advisories.missing_control: An independent scanner over our own security code.
advisories.fix: Each secret pattern has a name; a finding says which kind it found ("credential shape: an Anthropic key") and never repeats a character of it.
advisories.prevention: GitHub code scanning (CodeQL) now runs on every push, and push protection blocks supported secrets before they reach the repository.
